comment.body: Thanks for the 0.103.3052 update and the distinction between normal and service mode. That narrows the regression matrix, but success without service mode does not establish that the pairing problem is fixed generally. #51789 remains the open, unmerged candidate for the signer-verification issue. Candidate validation should use a consistent signed build on both computers and cover Use Service both off and on. There is no need to repeat the firewall checks already documented here, and mixing executables from different releases should not be treated as a supported repair.

actions.label: Retain service-mode regression with signer fix

title: Mouse Without Borders fails to pair: "Could not load or update pairing" (Negotiation → Connecting → Error)

judgment.recommended_action: Keep #51789 as the existing candidate; preserve the new normal-versus-service observation without recommending binary replacement or bypassing verification.
judgment.rationale: The latest reply does not supersede the existing fix: it distinguishes matching signer combinations in one preview from correctness of service-mode peer verification. Retain the report under the existing candidate and add normal/service mode to its consistent-build regression matrix. Do not equate preview non-service success with a shipped universal fix.
evidence: The original report already excludes several network, firewall, key and elevation explanations; later discussion supplies explicit untrusted-signature rejection.

The November 3 reply reports that preview 0.103.3052 works without service mode but fails when Use Service is enabled, and attributes the difference to the service executable signer. This is participant-reported behavior and certificate analysis, not an independent installation/signature test.
The contributor explicitly linked PR #51789 as the signer-policy candidate. Its current open/unmerged state and intended independent trusted-Microsoft signature checks remain applicable.
Earlier mixed-version executable workarounds have both positive and negative reports. They do not establish a supported or durable repair.
